## Comprehensive Shoring and Scaffolding Plan: Level 2 Suspended Slab

**Project Title:** Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition
**Project Location:** 10441 - 132 Street, Surrey, British Columbia, Canada
**Client/Contractor:** DC Forming Ltd.
**Drawing Title:** Level 2 Suspended Slab Shoring Plan & Details
**Drawing Number:** F-2
**Date of Issue:** November 04, 2025
**Revision Date:** November 12, 2025
**Prepared By:** F.T. (Drafter)
**Engineering Firm:** Greuter Engineering Ltd.
**EGBC Permit No.:** 1002364
**Engineering File No.:** GE-3548-1
**Scaffolding Supplier:** TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd.
**Contact Information:**
*   Website: www.ttfscaffolding.com
*   Telephone: 778-898-5301
*   Email: info@ttfscaffolding.com

---

### 1.0 Project Overview and Scope

This document details the shoring and scaffolding requirements for the Level 2 suspended concrete slab and associated structural elements at the Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition project. The scope includes the provision, installation, and dismantling of all temporary support structures necessary to safely construct the suspended concrete slab, slab bands, and reinforced concrete beams. This plan outlines specific material requirements, dimensional layouts, load capacities, installation procedures, and critical safety and engineering compliance notes. All work shall be performed in strict accordance with this document, relevant architectural and structural drawings, and applicable local and national building codes and safety regulations.

### 2.0 Structural Specifications and Elements

This section provides detailed descriptions of the permanent and temporary structural elements involved in the Level 2 suspended slab construction.

#### 2.1 Permanent Structural Elements to be Supported:

*   **10.5-inch (267 mm) Deep Suspended Slab (Typical, Unless Noted Otherwise - U.N.O.):** This refers to the standard thickness of the concrete floor slab for Level 2. The shoring system must be designed to support the wet weight of this concrete, formwork, live loads during concrete placement, and any associated construction loads.
*   **24-inch (610 mm) Deep Slab Band (Typical, U.N.O.):** Slab bands are thickened portions of the concrete slab, typically acting as shallow beams, designed to carry heavier loads or span longer distances. These areas require specific attention in shoring design due to their increased depth and corresponding higher weight per linear foot.
*   **300 mm x 450 mm Deep Reinforced Concrete (R/C) Beam:** These are primary structural beams, measuring 300 millimeters (approximately 11.8 inches) in width and 450 millimeters (approximately 17.7 inches) in depth, cast from reinforced concrete. The shoring system must provide continuous and robust support for the entire length of these beams during concrete placement and curing.
*   **300 mm x 500 mm Deep Reinforced Concrete (R/C) Beam:** These are larger primary structural beams, measuring 300 millimeters (approximately 11.8 inches) in width and 500 millimeters (approximately 19.7 inches) in depth, cast from reinforced concrete. These beams will impose greater loads on the shoring system compared to the 300x450mm beams due to their increased volume and weight.

#### 2.2 Temporary Shoring and Scaffolding Elements:

*   **Heavy-Duty Frame Scaffolding (Typical, U.N.O.):**
    *   **Dimensions:** All standard scaffolding frames shall be 5 feet (1.52 meters) high by 4 feet (1.22 meters) wide. These frames are designed to be stacked, with each "5'+5'" indicating two 5-foot high frames stacked to achieve a 10-foot working height, adjustable with screw jacks.
    *   **Load Capacity:** Each leg of the heavy-duty frame scaffolding system is engineered to support a maximum axial load of 10 kips (10,000 pounds or approximately 4,536 kilograms). This high load capacity is critical for safely supporting the significant weight of wet concrete, formwork, and construction live loads.
    *   **Bracing:** Each frame assembly shall be diagonally braced using 7-foot (2.13 meters) long cross-braces. This bracing is essential for ensuring the stability and rigidity of the scaffolding tower, preventing racking and lateral movement under load. Bracing must be installed at every level of stacked frames.
*   **Post Shores (Adjustable Steel Props):**
    *   **#2 Post Shore (Marked "X"):** These are heavy-duty adjustable steel post shores, specifically designated for areas requiring concentrated support or where frame scaffolding is impractical. Locations for #2 post shores are explicitly marked with an "X" on the shoring plan.
    *   **#3 Post Shore (Marked "[X]"):** These are medium-duty adjustable steel post shores, used for intermediate support or in conjunction with frame scaffolding. Locations for #3 post shores are explicitly marked with an "[X]" on the shoring plan.
    *   **#4 Post Shore (Marked "(&)"):** These are light-duty adjustable steel post shores, typically used for localized support or infill areas. Locations for #4 post shores are explicitly marked with a "(&)" on the shoring plan.
    *   **Purpose:** Post shores provide versatile, adjustable vertical support, particularly useful for varying slab heights, localized heavy loads, or where access for full frame scaffolding is restricted.
*   **Screw Jack Base Plates:**
    *   **Application:** These adjustable base plates are required at the bottom of all 4-foot (1.22 meter) high frame scaffolding assemblies.
    *   **Function:** The screw jack mechanism allows for fine adjustment of the frame height, ensuring the top of the shoring system is precisely level and at the correct elevation to support the formwork. The base plate distributes the concentrated load from the frame leg over a larger area onto the supporting surface (e.g., mudsills, concrete slab below).
*   **U-Head Plates (U-Head Jacks):**
    *   **Application:** These adjustable U-shaped head plates are required at the top of all 4-foot (1.22 meter) high frame scaffolding assemblies.
    *   **Function:** The U-head plate provides a stable cradle for supporting primary timber stringers or beams (e.g., 4x6 wood joists) directly above the scaffold frame. Like the base plate, it incorporates a screw jack for precise vertical adjustment, allowing the formwork to be set to the exact required elevation and camber.

### 3.0 Material Requirements and Quality Standards

All materials used for shoring and formwork shall meet the following specifications to ensure structural integrity and safety.

#### 3.1 Timber Formwork Components:

*   **Plywood Sheathing:**
    *   **Minimum Specification:** 3/4-inch (19 mm) thick, Douglas Fir (D. Fir) Grade #1 or better.
    *   **Purpose:** The plywood forms the direct contact surface for the concrete, providing a smooth finish and containing the wet concrete during placement and initial curing. Grade #1 or better Douglas Fir plywood ensures high strength, durability, and resistance to deflection under the weight of concrete.
*   **Wood Joists (Primary Decking Support):**
    *   **Specification:** 4-inch by 6-inch (102 mm x 152 mm) dimensional lumber joists. These shall be heavy-duty, structural grade lumber, free from significant defects such as large knots, splits, or excessive wane that could compromise their load-bearing capacity.
    *   **Length:** 12-foot (3.66 meters) standard length.
    *   **Spacing:** Spaced at 19.2 inches (488 mm) on center (O/C). This spacing is critical for distributing the slab load uniformly to the underlying shoring system and preventing excessive deflection of the plywood sheathing.
    *   **Supplier Note:** All 4x6 wood joists supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. are specifically intended for their structural role as formwork support. They **shall not** be used for packing, blocking, shims, or cut short for any other purpose that deviates from their intended structural application as defined in this plan. Misuse can compromise the structural integrity of the shoring system.
*   **Wood Joists (Under Steps):**
    *   **Specification:** Similar to the primary decking joists, 4-inch by 6-inch (102 mm x 152 mm) dimensional lumber, heavy-duty structural grade.
    *   **Spacing:** Spaced at 19.2 inches (488 mm) on center (O/C) specifically under the slab areas designated for stairs. This ensures consistent support for the stepped formwork.

#### 3.2 Scaffolding and Shoring Components:

*   **Scaffolding Frames:** Heavy-duty steel frame components, specifically engineered for shoring applications, with a certified load capacity of 10 kips (10,000 pounds) per leg. Frames must be free from rust, significant dents, or damage that could impair their structural performance.
*   **Cross Braces:** 7-foot (2.13 meters) long steel cross braces, designed to fit the specified scaffolding frames, ensuring proper connection and rigidity.
*   **Screw Jacks (Base and U-Head):** Heavy-duty steel screw jacks with robust threads and adjustment mechanisms, capable of supporting the specified loads and providing precise elevation control. Base plates must be adequately sized to distribute loads. U-head plates must securely cradle the timber joists.
*   **Post Shores:** Adjustable steel post shores (#2, #3, #4 types) with clearly marked load capacities and intact locking mechanisms. Each post shore must be inspected for damage, deformation, or corrosion prior to use.

### 4.0 Dimensions and Elevations

This section details the critical dimensions and elevations for the Level 2 shoring system, essential for accurate construction and alignment. All dimensions are in feet and inches unless otherwise specified.

#### 4.1 General Layout Dimensions:

The plan indicates various horizontal dimensions for the overall layout of the shoring, including:
*   **10'-6" (3.20 meters):** Repeated dimension, likely indicating bay widths or module lengths for the scaffolding frames.
*   **16'-0" (4.88 meters):** Various span lengths or spacing between major support lines.
*   **14'-0" (4.27 meters):** Various span lengths or spacing between major support lines.
*   **20'-0" (6.10 meters):** A larger span or section length.
*   **40'-6" (12.34 meters):** A significant overall dimension, likely a main axis or length of a structural element.
*   **5'-0" (1.52 meters):** Typical width of a bay or a specific offset.
*   **9'-3" (2.82 meters):** A specific offset or dimension for a structural feature.
*   **44'-0" (13.41 meters):** A major overall dimension, possibly the total length or width of a shored area.

These dimensions define the grid and placement of the shoring towers and individual post shores, ensuring adequate support throughout the slab area. The contractor must verify all dimensions on site prior to equipment shipment and installation.

#### 4.2 Vertical Elevations:

*   **EL. 89.95m (Elevation 89.95 meters):** This represents a critical elevation point, likely the top of the finished concrete slab or the top of the formwork at a specific location. All shoring components must be adjusted to ensure the formwork achieves this precise elevation, accounting for any required camber or deflection. This elevation is relative to the project's established vertical datum.

#### 4.3 Spacing and Distribution:

*   **@ 19.2" O/C (19.2 inches On Center):** This specifies the maximum center-to-center spacing for the 4x6 wood joists. This precise spacing (488 mm) is crucial for distributing the load from the concrete slab uniformly onto the underlying shoring system and for limiting deflection of the plywood formwork to acceptable tolerances. This spacing is also applied to joists supporting the formwork for sloped areas such as stairs.

### 5.0 Load Specifications

Accurate load calculations are fundamental to the safe design and installation of any shoring system. This section outlines the design loads considered for the Level 2 suspended slab.

#### 5.1 Distributed Area Loads:

*   **182 Pounds per Square Foot (P.S.F.):** This is the design load for the typical 10.5-inch (267 mm) deep suspended concrete slab. This value accounts for the self-weight of the wet concrete (approximately 150 lbs/cu.ft.), the weight of the formwork, and an allowance for construction live loads (e.g., workers, equipment, concrete buggies, material stockpiles).
*   **350 Pounds per Square Foot (P.S.F.):** This is the design load for the 24-inch (610 mm) deep slab bands. Due to their increased thickness, these areas generate significantly higher loads per square foot. This value similarly includes the self-weight of the wet concrete, formwork, and construction live loads, reflecting the additional structural demands in these areas.

#### 5.2 Concentrated Point Loads:

*   **10 Kips (10,000 pounds or 4,536 kilograms) per Leg:** This is the maximum permissible axial load capacity for each individual leg of the heavy-duty frame scaffolding system. This rating is a critical safety parameter, ensuring that the scaffolding components can safely support the distributed loads from the slab and beams when concentrated through the joist and stringer system. The total load on any scaffold tower must not exceed the sum of the capacities of its individual legs.

### 6.0 Installation Requirements

This section provides critical instructions for the proper installation of the shoring system. Adherence to these guidelines is mandatory for safety and structural performance.

#### 6.1 General Shoring Placement:

*   **Selective Shoring:** No shoring is required under the typical 10.5-inch slab nor under the 24-inch slab bands unless explicitly shown on the plan or marked with specific symbols.
    *   **"X" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #2 Post Shores (heavy-duty) are specifically required.
    *   **"[X]" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #3 Post Shores (medium-duty) are specifically required.
    *   **"(&)" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #4 Post Shores (light-duty) are specifically required.
*   **Purpose:** This selective shoring approach optimizes material usage and installation time by focusing support where it is structurally necessary, based on engineering analysis of slab spans, beam locations, and load concentrations.

#### 6.2 Specific Frame Installation Details:

*   **4-Foot (1.22 meter) High Frames:** For all scaffolding assemblies utilizing 4-foot high frames (either as the bottom tier or as part of a multi-tier stack), the following components are mandatory:
    *   **Screw Jack Base Plate (Bottom):** A screw jack base plate must be installed at the bottom of each leg of the frame to provide adjustable height control and to distribute the load to the supporting surface below (e.g., existing slab, mudsills).
    *   **U-Head Plate (Top):** A U-head plate (U-head jack) must be installed at the top of each leg of the frame to provide adjustable height control and to securely cradle the primary timber joists or stringers that support the formwork.

#### 6.3 Contractor-Supplied Build-Ups:

*   **Build Up Under Slab (By Contractor):** In areas where the existing supporting surface (e.g., grade, lower slab) is below the required base elevation for the shoring system, the contractor is responsible for constructing stable "build-ups." These build-ups may consist of compacted granular fill, timber cribbing, or concrete pads, designed to provide a level, firm, and adequately strong foundation for the shoring base plates. The design and construction of these build-ups must be reviewed and approved by the project's Professional Engineer.
*   **Build Up Under Slope for Stairs (By Contractor):** Similarly, for areas supporting the formwork for stairs or sloped slabs, the contractor is responsible for constructing appropriate build-ups or stepped foundations to accommodate the varying heights of the shoring system. These build-ups must be robust, level, and capable of transferring all shoring loads safely to the ground or supporting structure.

### 7.0 Safety and Compliance Notes

Safety is paramount in all construction activities, especially with temporary structures like shoring. Strict adherence to these notes is mandatory.

#### 7.1 Engineering Inspection and Approval:

*   **Mandatory Inspection:** An inspection by the undersigned Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) from Greuter Engineering Ltd. is **mandatorily required** prior to any concrete pouring operations for the Level 2 suspended slab. This inspection will verify that the shoring and formwork have been installed correctly, conform to the approved drawings, and are safe to support the concrete pour.
*   **Notice Requirement:** The contractor shall provide a minimum of **48 hours advance notice** to Greuter Engineering Ltd. to schedule this inspection. Failure to provide adequate notice may result in delays to the concrete pour.

#### 7.2 Drawing Coordination and Verification:

*   **Read in Conjunction:** This shoring plan drawing (F-2) shall always be read and interpreted in conjunction with all relevant architectural and structural drawings for the project. Discrepancies or conflicts between drawings must be immediately brought to the attention of the Project Manager and the Professional Engineer for clarification before proceeding with work.
*   **Contractor Verification:** The contractor is solely responsible for checking and confirming all dimensions, elevations, and site conditions prior to the shipment of scaffolding and shoring equipment and prior to commencing installation. Any discrepancies between site conditions and the drawings must be reported immediately to the Professional Engineer.

#### 7.3 Material Usage Restrictions:

*   **Dedicated Use of 4x6 Joists:** The 4x6 wood joists supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. are specifically designated for their structural role as primary formwork supports. They are **strictly prohibited** from being used for any other purpose, including but not limited to:
    *   Packing or shimming under base plates or frames.
    *   Cutting short for non-structural blocking or bracing.
    *   Use as temporary access planks or platforms.
    *   Any other application that might compromise their structural integrity or intended use.
    *   **Rationale:** Misuse of these structural components can lead to overloading, premature failure, and catastrophic collapse of the shoring system.

#### 7.4 General Safety Practices:

*   **Competent Person:** All shoring and scaffolding erection, alteration, and dismantling shall be supervised by a competent person as defined by occupational health and safety regulations.
*   **Fall Protection:** Appropriate fall protection systems shall be utilized by all personnel working at heights during the erection and dismantling of scaffolding.
*   **Access:** Safe access to all work areas on the scaffolding shall be provided and maintained.
*   **Site Conditions:** The ground or supporting slab beneath the shoring must be level, firm, and capable of supporting the anticipated loads without settlement. Mud sills or sole plates shall be used as required to distribute loads.
*   **Plumb and Level:** All shoring frames and post shores must be erected plumb and level, with all connections secured as per manufacturer's instructions.
*   **Weather Protection:** During adverse weather conditions (e.g., high winds, heavy rain, freezing temperatures), additional precautions or cessation of work may be required.
*   **Load Management:** No concentrated loads, material stockpiles, or equipment exceeding the design capacity shall be placed on the formwork or shoring system.

### 8.0 Engineering Requirements

The design and implementation of this shoring plan are governed by specific engineering principles and requirements to ensure the safety and stability of the temporary structure.

#### 8.1 Design Authority:

*   **Professional Engineer:** This shoring plan has been prepared and reviewed by a Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) registered with Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC), operating under Permit No. 1002364. The design adheres to all applicable Canadian building codes, engineering standards, and safety regulations.
*   **Design Basis:** The design accounts for all relevant dead loads (self-weight of concrete, formwork, rebar) and live loads (construction personnel, equipment, impact loads, material stockpiles) as specified in Section 5.0. It also considers factors such as concrete pour sequence, lateral stability, and potential environmental loads.

#### 8.2 Design File and Documentation:

*   **Project File:** All calculations, design assumptions, and supporting documentation for this shoring plan are maintained under Greuter Engineering Ltd. file number GE-3548-1. This file is available for review by authorized personnel upon request.

#### 8.3 Post-Pour Stripping and Reshoring:

*   **Engineer's Direction:** The schedule and sequence for stripping formwork and removing shoring, as well as any requirements for reshoring (if applicable), shall be determined by the Professional Engineer based on concrete strength gain (verified by field tests) and the structural design of the permanent elements. No shoring shall be removed without explicit written authorization from the Engineer of Record.

### 9.0 Quality Standards

All materials and workmanship shall meet the highest industry quality standards to ensure the integrity and safety of the shoring system.

#### 9.1 Material Grades and Certifications:

*   **Plywood:** Minimum 3/4-inch (19 mm) thick, Douglas Fir (D. Fir) #1 Grade or better, conforming to CSA O121 or equivalent North American standards for structural plywood. Plywood must be free from delamination, excessive warping, or damage.
*   **Dimensional Lumber (4x6 Joists):** Structural grade lumber, minimum No. 2 Grade or better, conforming to NLGA (National Lumber Grades Authority) grading rules for Canadian lumber or equivalent. Lumber must be visually inspected for defects such as large knots, splits, checks, or decay that could reduce its strength.
*   **Scaffolding Components:** All steel scaffolding frames, braces, screw jacks, and post shores must be manufactured from high-strength steel, conforming to relevant CSA (Canadian Standards Association) or ANSI (American National Standards Institute) standards for scaffolding. Components must be certified by the manufacturer for their stated load capacities and be free from excessive corrosion, deformation, or weld defects.

#### 9.2 Workmanship:

*   **Skilled Labor:** All shoring and formwork shall be erected by experienced and qualified personnel under the direct supervision of a competent person.
*   **Accuracy:** All components shall be installed to the specified dimensions and elevations with a tolerance of +/- 1/4 inch (6 mm) for critical dimensions and elevations.
*   **Connections:** All connections, including frame pins, brace locks, and screw jack adjustments, shall be securely fastened and inspected prior to loading.
*   **Stability:** The entire shoring system shall be erected plumb, level, and adequately braced to ensure stability against lateral loads and overturning.

---
**END OF DOCUMENT**

This section provides detailed descriptions of the permanent and temporary structural elements involved in the Level 2 suspended slab construction.
#### 2.1 Permanent Structural Elements to be Supported:

*   **10.5-inch (267 mm) Deep Suspended Slab (Typical, Unless Noted Otherwise - U.N.O.):** This refers to the standard thickness of the concrete floor slab for Level 2. The shoring system must be designed to support the wet weight of this concrete, formwork, live loads during concrete placement, and any associated construction loads.

*   **24-inch (610 mm) Deep Slab Band (Typical, U.N.O.):** Slab bands are thickened portions of the concrete slab, typically acting as shallow beams, designed to carry heavier loads or span longer distances. These areas require specific attention in shoring design due to their increased depth and corresponding higher weight per linear foot.

*   **300 mm x 450 mm Deep Reinforced Concrete (R/C) Beam:** These are primary structural beams, measuring 300 millimeters (approximately 11.8 inches) in width and 450 millimeters (approximately 17.7 inches) in depth, cast from reinforced concrete. The shoring system must provide continuous and robust support for the entire length of these beams during concrete placement and curing.

*   **300 mm x 500 mm Deep Reinforced Concrete (R/C) Beam:** These are larger primary structural beams, measuring 300 millimeters (approximately 11.8 inches) in width and 500 millimeters (approximately 19.7 inches) in depth, cast from reinforced concrete. These beams will impose greater loads on the shoring system compared to the 300x450mm beams due to their increased volume and weight.

*   **Dimensions:** All standard scaffolding frames shall be 5 feet (1.52 meters) high by 4 feet (1.22 meters) wide. These frames are designed to be stacked, with each "5'+5'" indicating two 5-foot high frames stacked to achieve a 10-foot working height, adjustable with screw jacks.

*   **Load Capacity:** Each leg of the heavy-duty frame scaffolding system is engineered to support a maximum axial load of 10 kips (10,000 pounds or approximately 4,536 kilograms). This high load capacity is critical for safely supporting the significant weight of wet concrete, formwork, and construction live loads.

*   **Bracing:** Each frame assembly shall be diagonally braced using 7-foot (2.13 meters) long cross-braces. This bracing is essential for ensuring the stability and rigidity of the scaffolding tower, preventing racking and lateral movement under load. Bracing must be installed at every level of stacked frames.

*   **#2 Post Shore (Marked "X"):** These are heavy-duty adjustable steel post shores, specifically designated for areas requiring concentrated support or where frame scaffolding is impractical. Locations for #2 post shores are explicitly marked with an "X" on the shoring plan.

*   **#3 Post Shore (Marked "[X]"):** These are medium-duty adjustable steel post shores, used for intermediate support or in conjunction with frame scaffolding. Locations for #3 post shores are explicitly marked with an "[X]" on the shoring plan.

*   **#4 Post Shore (Marked "(&)"):** These are light-duty adjustable steel post shores, typically used for localized support or infill areas. Locations for #4 post shores are explicitly marked with a "(&)" on the shoring plan.

*   **Purpose:** Post shores provide versatile, adjustable vertical support, particularly useful for varying slab heights, localized heavy loads, or where access for full frame scaffolding is restricted.
*   **Application:** These adjustable base plates are required at the bottom of all 4-foot (1.22 meter) high frame scaffolding assemblies.

*   **Function:** The screw jack mechanism allows for fine adjustment of the frame height, ensuring the top of the shoring system is precisely level and at the correct elevation to support the formwork. The base plate distributes the concentrated load from the frame leg over a larger area onto the supporting surface (e.g., mudsills, concrete slab below).
*   **Application:** These adjustable U-shaped head plates are required at the top of all 4-foot (1.22 meter) high frame scaffolding assemblies.

*   **Function:** The U-head plate provides a stable cradle for supporting primary timber stringers or beams (e.g., 4x6 wood joists) directly above the scaffold frame. Like the base plate, it incorporates a screw jack for precise vertical adjustment, allowing the formwork to be set to the exact required elevation and camber.
All materials used for shoring and formwork shall meet the following specifications to ensure structural integrity and safety.
*   **Minimum Specification:** 3/4-inch (19 mm) thick, Douglas Fir (D. Fir) Grade #1 or better.

*   **Purpose:** The plywood forms the direct contact surface for the concrete, providing a smooth finish and containing the wet concrete during placement and initial curing. Grade #1 or better Douglas Fir plywood ensures high strength, durability, and resistance to deflection under the weight of concrete.

*   **Specification:** 4-inch by 6-inch (102 mm x 152 mm) dimensional lumber joists. These shall be heavy-duty, structural grade lumber, free from significant defects such as large knots, splits, or excessive wane that could compromise their load-bearing capacity.

*   **Spacing:** Spaced at 19.2 inches (488 mm) on center (O/C). This spacing is critical for distributing the slab load uniformly to the underlying shoring system and preventing excessive deflection of the plywood sheathing.

*   **Supplier Note:** All 4x6 wood joists supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. are specifically intended for their structural role as formwork support. They **shall not** be used for packing, blocking, shims, or cut short for any other purpose that deviates from their intended structural application as defined in this plan. Misuse can compromise the structural integrity of the shoring system.
*   **Specification:** Similar to the primary decking joists, 4-inch by 6-inch (102 mm x 152 mm) dimensional lumber, heavy-duty structural grade.
*   **Spacing:** Spaced at 19.2 inches (488 mm) on center (O/C) specifically under the slab areas designated for stairs. This ensures consistent support for the stepped formwork.

*   **Scaffolding Frames:** Heavy-duty steel frame components, specifically engineered for shoring applications, with a certified load capacity of 10 kips (10,000 pounds) per leg. Frames must be free from rust, significant dents, or damage that could impair their structural performance.
*   **Cross Braces:** 7-foot (2.13 meters) long steel cross braces, designed to fit the specified scaffolding frames, ensuring proper connection and rigidity.

*   **Screw Jacks (Base and U-Head):** Heavy-duty steel screw jacks with robust threads and adjustment mechanisms, capable of supporting the specified loads and providing precise elevation control. Base plates must be adequately sized to distribute loads. U-head plates must securely cradle the timber joists.

*   **Post Shores:** Adjustable steel post shores (#2, #3, #4 types) with clearly marked load capacities and intact locking mechanisms. Each post shore must be inspected for damage, deformation, or corrosion prior to use.

This section details the critical dimensions and elevations for the Level 2 shoring system, essential for accurate construction and alignment. All dimensions are in feet and inches unless otherwise specified.
The plan indicates various horizontal dimensions for the overall layout of the shoring, including:
*   **10'-6" (3.20 meters):** Repeated dimension, likely indicating bay widths or module lengths for the scaffolding frames.
*   **16'-0" (4.88 meters):** Various span lengths or spacing between major support lines.
*   **14'-0" (4.27 meters):** Various span lengths or spacing between major support lines.
*   **20'-0" (6.10 meters):** A larger span or section length.
*   **40'-6" (12.34 meters):** A significant overall dimension, likely a main axis or length of a structural element.
*   **5'-0" (1.52 meters):** Typical width of a bay or a specific offset.
*   **9'-3" (2.82 meters):** A specific offset or dimension for a structural feature.
*   **44'-0" (13.41 meters):** A major overall dimension, possibly the total length or width of a shored area.

These dimensions define the grid and placement of the shoring towers and individual post shores, ensuring adequate support throughout the slab area. The contractor must verify all dimensions on site prior to equipment shipment and installation.

*   **EL. 89.95m (Elevation 89.95 meters):** This represents a critical elevation point, likely the top of the finished concrete slab or the top of the formwork at a specific location. All shoring components must be adjusted to ensure the formwork achieves this precise elevation, accounting for any required camber or deflection. This elevation is relative to the project's established vertical datum.

*   **@ 19.2" O/C (19.2 inches On Center):** This specifies the maximum center-to-center spacing for the 4x6 wood joists. This precise spacing (488 mm) is crucial for distributing the load from the concrete slab uniformly onto the underlying shoring system and for limiting deflection of the plywood formwork to acceptable tolerances. This spacing is also applied to joists supporting the formwork for sloped areas such as stairs.
Accurate load calculations are fundamental to the safe design and installation of any shoring system. This section outlines the design loads considered for the Level 2 suspended slab.

*   **182 Pounds per Square Foot (P.S.F.):** This is the design load for the typical 10.5-inch (267 mm) deep suspended concrete slab. This value accounts for the self-weight of the wet concrete (approximately 150 lbs/cu.ft.), the weight of the formwork, and an allowance for construction live loads (e.g., workers, equipment, concrete buggies, material stockpiles).

*   **350 Pounds per Square Foot (P.S.F.):** This is the design load for the 24-inch (610 mm) deep slab bands. Due to their increased thickness, these areas generate significantly higher loads per square foot. This value similarly includes the self-weight of the wet concrete, formwork, and construction live loads, reflecting the additional structural demands in these areas.

*   **10 Kips (10,000 pounds or 4,536 kilograms) per Leg:** This is the maximum permissible axial load capacity for each individual leg of the heavy-duty frame scaffolding system. This rating is a critical safety parameter, ensuring that the scaffolding components can safely support the distributed loads from the slab and beams when concentrated through the joist and stringer system. The total load on any scaffold tower must not exceed the sum of the capacities of its individual legs.
This section provides critical instructions for the proper installation of the shoring system. Adherence to these guidelines is mandatory for safety and structural performance.
*   **Selective Shoring:** No shoring is required under the typical 10.5-inch slab nor under the 24-inch slab bands unless explicitly shown on the plan or marked with specific symbols.
*   **"X" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #2 Post Shores (heavy-duty) are specifically required.
*   **"[X]" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #3 Post Shores (medium-duty) are specifically required.
*   **"(&)" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #4 Post Shores (light-duty) are specifically required.

*   **Purpose:** This selective shoring approach optimizes material usage and installation time by focusing support where it is structurally necessary, based on engineering analysis of slab spans, beam locations, and load concentrations.

*   **4-Foot (1.22 meter) High Frames:** For all scaffolding assemblies utilizing 4-foot high frames (either as the bottom tier or as part of a multi-tier stack), the following components are mandatory:

*   **Screw Jack Base Plate (Bottom):** A screw jack base plate must be installed at the bottom of each leg of the frame to provide adjustable height control and to distribute the load to the supporting surface below (e.g., existing slab, mudsills).

*   **U-Head Plate (Top):** A U-head plate (U-head jack) must be installed at the top of each leg of the frame to provide adjustable height control and to securely cradle the primary timber joists or stringers that support the formwork.

*   **Build Up Under Slab (By Contractor):** In areas where the existing supporting surface (e.g., grade, lower slab) is below the required base elevation for the shoring system, the contractor is responsible for constructing stable "build-ups." The design and construction of these build-ups must be reviewed and approved by the project's Professional Engineer.

*   **Build Up Under Slope for Stairs (By Contractor):** Similarly, for areas supporting the formwork for stairs or sloped slabs, the contractor is responsible for constructing appropriate build-ups or stepped foundations to accommodate the varying heights of the shoring system. Eng.) from Greuter Engineering Ltd. is **mandatorily required** prior to any concrete pouring operations for the Level 2 suspended slab. Discrepancies or conflicts between drawings must be immediately brought to the attention of the Project Manager and the Professional Engineer for clarification before proceeding with work.

*   **Contractor Verification:** The contractor is solely responsible for checking and confirming all dimensions, elevations, and site conditions prior to the shipment of scaffolding and shoring equipment and prior to commencing installation. Any discrepancies between site conditions and the drawings must be reported immediately to the Professional Engineer.

*   **Dedicated Use of 4x6 Joists:** The 4x6 wood joists supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. are specifically designated for their structural role as primary formwork supports. They are **strictly prohibited** from being used for any other purpose, including but not limited to:
*   Packing or shimming under base plates or frames.
*   Cutting short for non-structural blocking or bracing.
*   Use as temporary access planks or platforms.
*   Any other application that might compromise their structural integrity or intended use.

*   **Competent Person:** All shoring and scaffolding erection, alteration, and dismantling shall be supervised by a competent person as defined by occupational health and safety regulations.
*   **Fall Protection:** Appropriate fall protection systems shall be utilized by all personnel working at heights during the erection and dismantling of scaffolding.
*   **Access:** Safe access to all work areas on the scaffolding shall be provided and maintained.

*   **Site Conditions:** The ground or supporting slab beneath the shoring must be level, firm, and capable of supporting the anticipated loads without settlement. Mud sills or sole plates shall be used as required to distribute loads.
*   **Plumb and Level:** All shoring frames and post shores must be erected plumb and level, with all connections secured as per manufacturer's instructions.
*   **Weather Protection:** During adverse weather conditions (e.g., high winds, heavy rain, freezing temperatures), additional precautions or cessation of work may be required.
*   **Load Management:** No concentrated loads, material stockpiles, or equipment exceeding the design capacity shall be placed on the formwork or shoring system.
The design and implementation of this shoring plan are governed by specific engineering principles and requirements to ensure the safety and stability of the temporary structure.

*   **Professional Engineer:** This shoring plan has been prepared and reviewed by a Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) registered with Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC), operating under Permit No. 1002364. The design adheres to all applicable Canadian building codes, engineering standards, and safety regulations.

*   **Design Basis:** The design accounts for all relevant dead loads (self-weight of concrete, formwork, rebar) and live loads (construction personnel, equipment, impact loads, material stockpiles) as specified in Section 5.0. It also considers factors such as concrete pour sequence, lateral stability, and potential environmental loads.

*   **Project File:** All calculations, design assumptions, and supporting documentation for this shoring plan are maintained under Greuter Engineering Ltd. file number GE-3548-1. This file is available for review by authorized personnel upon request.

*   **Engineer's Direction:** The schedule and sequence for stripping formwork and removing shoring, as well as any requirements for reshoring (if applicable), shall be determined by the Professional Engineer based on concrete strength gain (verified by field tests) and the structural design of the permanent elements. No shoring shall be removed without explicit written authorization from the Engineer of Record.
All materials and workmanship shall meet the highest industry quality standards to ensure the integrity and safety of the shoring system.

*   **Plywood:** Minimum 3/4-inch (19 mm) thick, Douglas Fir (D. Fir) #1 Grade or better, conforming to CSA O121 or equivalent North American standards for structural plywood. Plywood must be free from delamination, excessive warping, or damage.

*   **Dimensional Lumber (4x6 Joists):** Structural grade lumber, minimum No. 2 Grade or better, conforming to NLGA (National Lumber Grades Authority) grading rules for Canadian lumber or equivalent. Lumber must be visually inspected for defects such as large knots, splits, checks, or decay that could reduce its strength.

*   **Scaffolding Components:** All steel scaffolding frames, braces, screw jacks, and post shores must be manufactured from high-strength steel, conforming to relevant CSA (Canadian Standards Association) or ANSI (American National Standards Institute) standards for scaffolding. Components must be certified by the manufacturer for their stated load capacities and be free from excessive corrosion, deformation, or weld defects.
*   **Skilled Labor:** All shoring and formwork shall be erected by experienced and qualified personnel under the direct supervision of a competent person.
*   **Accuracy:** All components shall be installed to the specified dimensions and elevations with a tolerance of +/- 1/4 inch (6 mm) for critical dimensions and elevations.
*   **Connections:** All connections, including frame pins, brace locks, and screw jack adjustments, shall be securely fastened and inspected prior to loading.
*   **Stability:** The entire shoring system shall be erected plumb, level, and adequately braced to ensure stability against lateral loads and overturning.

#### 5.2 Concentrated Point Loads:

*   **10 Kips (10,000 pounds or 4,536 kilograms) per Leg:** This is the maximum permissible axial load capacity for each individual leg of the heavy-duty frame scaffolding system. This rating is a critical safety parameter, ensuring that the scaffolding components can safely support the distributed loads from the slab and beams when concentrated through the joist and stringer system. The total load on any scaffold tower must not exceed the sum of the capacities of its individual legs.

### 6.0 Installation Requirements

This section provides critical instructions for the proper installation of the shoring system. Adherence to these guidelines is mandatory for safety and structural performance.

#### 6.1 General Shoring Placement:

*   **Selective Shoring:** No shoring is required under the typical 10.5-inch slab nor under the 24-inch slab bands unless explicitly shown on the plan or marked with specific symbols.
    *   **"X" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #2 Post Shores (heavy-duty) are specifically required.
    *   **"[X]" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #3 Post Shores (medium-duty) are specifically required.
    *   **"(&)" Symbol:** Indicates locations where #4 Post Shores (light-duty) are specifically required.
*   **Purpose:** This selective shoring approach optimizes material usage and installation time by focusing support where it is structurally necessary, based on engineering analysis of slab spans, beam locations, and load concentrations.

#### 6.2 Specific Frame Installation Details:

*   **4-Foot (1.22 meter) High Frames:** For all scaffolding assemblies utilizing 4-foot high frames (either as the bottom tier or as part of a multi-tier stack), the following components are mandatory:
    *   **Screw Jack Base Plate (Bottom):** A screw jack base plate must be installed at the bottom of each leg of the frame to provide adjustable height control and to distribute the load to the supporting surface below (e.g., existing slab, mudsills).
    *   **U-Head Plate (Top):** A U-head plate (U-head jack) must be installed at the top of each leg of the frame to provide adjustable height control and to securely cradle the primary timber joists or stringers that support the formwork.

#### 6.3 Contractor-Supplied Build-Ups:

*   **Build Up Under Slab (By Contractor):** In areas where the existing supporting surface (e.g., grade, lower slab) is below the required base elevation for the shoring system, the contractor is responsible for constructing stable "build-ups." These build-ups may consist of compacted granular fill, timber cribbing, or concrete pads, designed to provide a level, firm, and adequately strong foundation for the shoring base plates. The design and construction of these build-ups must be reviewed and approved by the project's Professional Engineer.
*   **Build Up Under Slope for Stairs (By Contractor):** Similarly, for areas supporting the formwork for stairs or sloped slabs, the contractor is responsible for constructing appropriate build-ups or stepped foundations to accommodate the varying heights of the shoring system. These build-ups must be robust, level, and capable of transferring all shoring loads safely to the ground or supporting structure.

### 7.0 Safety and Compliance Notes

Safety is paramount in all construction activities, especially with temporary structures like shoring. Strict adherence to these notes is mandatory.

#### 7.1 Engineering Inspection and Approval:

*   **Mandatory Inspection:** An inspection by the undersigned Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) from Greuter Engineering Ltd. is **mandatorily required** prior to any concrete pouring operations for the Level 2 suspended slab. This inspection will verify that the shoring and formwork have been installed correctly, conform to the approved drawings, and are safe to support the concrete pour.
*   **Notice Requirement:** The contractor shall provide a minimum of **48 hours advance notice** to Greuter Engineering Ltd. to schedule this inspection. Failure to provide adequate notice may result in delays to the concrete pour.

#### 7.2 Drawing Coordination and Verification:

*   **Read in Conjunction:** This shoring plan drawing (F-2) shall always be read and interpreted in conjunction with all relevant architectural and structural drawings for the project. Discrepancies or conflicts between drawings must be immediately brought to the attention of the Project Manager and the Professional Engineer for clarification before proceeding with work.
*   **Contractor Verification:** The contractor is solely responsible for checking and confirming all dimensions, elevations, and site conditions prior to the shipment of scaffolding and shoring equipment and prior to commencing installation. Any discrepancies between site conditions and the drawings must be reported immediately to the Professional Engineer.

#### 7.3 Material Usage Restrictions:

*   **Dedicated Use of 4x6 Joists:** The 4x6 wood joists supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. are specifically designated for their structural role as primary formwork supports. They are **strictly prohibited** from being used for any other purpose, including but not limited to:
    *   Packing or shimming under base plates or frames.
    *   Cutting short for non-structural blocking or bracing.
    *   Use as temporary access planks or platforms.
    *   Any other application that might compromise their structural integrity or intended use.
    *   **Rationale:** Misuse of these structural components can lead to overloading, premature failure, and catastrophic collapse of the shoring system.

#### 7.4 General Safety Practices:

*   **Competent Person:** All shoring and scaffolding erection, alteration, and dismantling shall be supervised by a competent person as defined by occupational health and safety regulations.
*   **Fall Protection:** Appropriate fall protection systems shall be utilized by all personnel working at heights during the erection and dismantling of scaffolding.
*   **Access:** Safe access to all work areas on the scaffolding shall be provided and maintained.
*   **Site Conditions:** The ground or supporting slab beneath the shoring must be level, firm, and capable of supporting the anticipated loads without settlement. Mud sills or sole plates shall be used as required to distribute loads.
*   **Plumb and Level:** All shoring frames and post shores must be erected plumb and level, with all connections secured as per manufacturer's instructions.
*   **Weather Protection:** During adverse weather conditions (e.g., high winds, heavy rain, freezing temperatures), additional precautions or cessation of work may be required.
*   **Load Management:** No concentrated loads, material stockpiles, or equipment exceeding the design capacity shall be placed on the formwork or shoring system.

### 8.0 Engineering Requirements

The design and implementation of this shoring plan are governed by specific engineering principles and requirements to ensure the safety and stability of the temporary structure.

#### 8.1 Design Authority:

*   **Professional Engineer:** This shoring plan has been prepared and reviewed by a Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) registered with Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC), operating under Permit No. 1002364. The design adheres to all applicable Canadian building codes, engineering standards, and safety regulations.
*   **Design Basis:** The design accounts for all relevant dead loads (self-weight of concrete, formwork, rebar) and live loads (construction personnel, equipment, impact loads, material stockpiles) as specified in Section 5.0. It also considers factors such as concrete pour sequence, lateral stability, and potential environmental loads.

#### 8.2 Design File and Documentation:

*   **Project File:** All calculations, design assumptions, and supporting documentation for this shoring plan are maintained under Greuter Engineering Ltd. file number GE-3548-1. This file is available for review by authorized personnel upon request.

#### 8.3 Post-Pour Stripping and Reshoring:

*   **Engineer's Direction:** The schedule and sequence for stripping formwork and removing shoring, as well as any requirements for reshoring (if applicable), shall be determined by the Professional Engineer based on concrete strength gain (verified by field tests) and the structural design of the permanent elements. No shoring shall be removed without explicit written authorization from the Engineer of Record.

### 9.0 Quality Standards

All materials and workmanship shall meet the highest industry quality standards to ensure the integrity and safety of the shoring system.

#### 9.1 Material Grades and Certifications:

*   **Plywood:** Minimum 3/4-inch (19 mm) thick, Douglas Fir (D. Fir) #1 Grade or better, conforming to CSA O121 or equivalent North American standards for structural plywood. Plywood must be free from delamination, excessive warping, or damage.
*   **Dimensional Lumber (4x6 Joists):** Structural grade lumber, minimum No. 2 Grade or better, conforming to NLGA (National Lumber Grades Authority) grading rules for Canadian lumber or equivalent. Lumber must be visually inspected for defects such as large knots, splits, checks, or decay that could reduce its strength.
*   **Scaffolding Components:** All steel scaffolding frames, braces, screw jacks, and post shores must be manufactured from high-strength steel, conforming to relevant CSA (Canadian Standards Association) or ANSI (American National Standards Institute) standards for scaffolding. Components must be certified by the manufacturer for their stated load capacities and be free from excessive corrosion, deformation, or weld defects.

#### 9.2 Workmanship:

*   **Skilled Labor:** All shoring and formwork shall be erected by experienced and qualified personnel under the direct supervision of a competent person.
*   **Accuracy:** All components shall be installed to the specified dimensions and elevations with a tolerance of +/- 1/4 inch (6 mm) for critical dimensions and elevations.
*   **Connections:** All connections, including frame pins, brace locks, and screw jack adjustments, shall be securely fastened and inspected prior to loading.
*   **Stability:** The entire shoring system shall be erected plumb, level, and adequately braced to ensure stability against lateral loads and overturning.
